mission: Ben wakes the three survivors. Sera orients first — disciplined and formal; Torin second — warm, commanding, steady; Kael last — quiet, watchful, saying nothing yet. Three people a thousand years out of their own time.
why_now: The containment is failing and the fortress is running out of vigil. The survivors are the only living source of context for what Gavran built and why.
conflict: The survivors are disoriented and wary in different ways. Sera demands identification and chain of command. Torin assesses Ben tactically with an ease that surprises him. Kael says nothing, and his silence is the loudest thing in the room.
turning_point: Sera recognises Ben as Jedi-trained but not of her era. 'What year is it?' Ben answers. The room holds its breath. All three register the number differently, and all three begin the private math of what a thousand years has cost them.
opening_hook: Ben's hand on the stasis release feels like a choice he can't take back. The first chamber's field dissolves, and a woman with the bearing of a soldier opens eyes that have been closed for a thousand years.
closing_hook: Torin is the last to orient. He looks at the nine dark chambers, the empty one, and says quietly: 'Who got out?'
emotional_trajectory: Tense anticipation -> the shock of contact across centuries -> growing dread as scope becomes apparent

stakes.personal: Ben has just assumed responsibility for three people a millennium out of time
stakes.interpersonal: The survivors' immediate trust dynamics — Sera demanding, Torin assessing, Kael retreating
stakes.external: These people are the only ones who understand what the fortress contains

setting: Fortress Level 3 — Stasis Ring, emergency lighting, the three active chambers
sensory_details: Stasis fields collapsing with a sound like held breath released; Sera's Force presence — sharp and disciplined, a signature shaped by an older training; Torin's — warm and heavy, something settled deep that Ben does not yet have a name for; Kael's — clipped and guarded, trained in a register Ben has not encountered before
canon_elements_needed: Millennium of temporal displacement effects on Force-sensitives
Jedi Lords era training versus modern Jedi training differences
Force presence perception of ancient practitioners by modern Jedi
Archaic Basic language and communication across eras
Stasis revival procedures and physiological recovery
action_beats: Ben pulls the stasis release lever — the first chamber's field dissolves with an audible hiss of released pressure
Sera Varik opens her eyes and immediately assumes a combat crouch before orientation hits
Torin Hal emerges from the second chamber, staggers, catches himself on the doorframe with one hand
Kael Drenn exits the third chamber in silence, back against the wall, scanning the room and cataloguing exits
promises_planted: Sera's formal distance from Ben will thaw (PP15)
Sera and Torin's thousand-year unresolved relationship will play out (PP03)
Sera's rigidity will break into principled flexibility, not abandonment (PP20)
notes: Ben's phase shifts here — the survivors' dependence gives his sense-of-burden a surface to land on. Sera, Torin, Kael all enter at their own lie_established. Survivor speech patterns: Sera speaks in complete sentences under stress — formal, precise, military. Torin's warmth has an archaic courtesy to it. Kael waits to be addressed; the silence itself is archaic. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, read Torin's signature as 'something slipping toward dark' or narrate the anchor architecture. He registers each survivor's presence as a body does: tone, weight, clipped edge. Interpretation waits for the archive. Note the three-signature contrast is the chapter's load-bearing image; keep it unhurried and specific, one line apiece, and do not stack metaphors on it.
